lead_with.text: PrognomiQ finds cancer signals in **plasma**. SLACS can isolate tumor, stroma and normal regions from **matched tissue** to show where a candidate protein comes from — evidence that strengthens a biomarker for clinical validation and FDA.

person.name: Joon-Yong Lee
person.text: Director of Bioinformatics at PrognomiQ since Oct 2023, working hybrid from Richland, WA. He **led bioinformatics for ProVue Lung** through analytical and clinical validation and launch, and runs multi-omics biomarker discovery with machine learning on LC-MS/MS proteomics, metabolomics, lipidomics and glycoproteomics (Seer Proteograph, timsTOF, ZenoTOF) on AWS pipelines. Joined PrognomiQ in Dec 2021 as Principal Data Scientist: built a cloud mass-spec platform; deep learning on raw MS data, patented (**US 12,387,508**). Before: **Pacific Northwest National Laboratory** 2014–2021 (postdoc, then staff scientist; tools LipidOz, Kaiko, AutoCCS, Blazing Signature Filter; CPTAC ovarian cancer proteomics), postdoc at Iowa State (2013–14), researcher at ATR Kyoto on the Honda ASIMO project (2011–13). PhD in Electrical Engineering, KAIST (2011).

company.text: PrognomiQ was spun out of **Seer** in September 2020 and is based in San Mateo, CA. It combines proteomics (Seer's Proteograph), metabolomics and genomics to build blood tests for cancer and other complex diseases. Its MOSAIC study of 2,513 subjects reported **89% sensitivity and 89% specificity** for lung cancer in validation, 80% at stage I. In November 2025 it launched **ProVue Lung**, an 11-protein blood LDT for high-risk adults, in an early experience program with Allegheny Health Network and Penn Highlands Healthcare. It plans an FDA-facing trial and a PMA. CEO: Philip Ma, PhD; VP Data Sciences: Manway Liu, PhD.

financials.text: **Sep 2020 — initial financing:** $55M, led by aMoon; Fidelity, T. Rowe Price, Invus, Maverick, Emerson Collective, Wing VC, Bruker. Seer kept ~19%. **Mar 2022:** $46M, led by Bruker with Catalio Capital — total $101M. **Nov 2024 — Series D:** $34M (Seer and Casdin Capital reported as leads). **Aug 2025:** Series D-II tranche, amount not disclosed. **Jan 2026:** ~$11.9M (SEC Form D), aMoon reported as lead. **Total disclosed:** ~$147M (CB Insights shows ~$157M incl. undisclosed tranche). Private company; no revenue published. ProVue Lung is in limited release, so revenue is likely small.

industry.title: Blood tests need tissue proof
industry.text: Proteomic liquid biopsy is moving to FDA trials. Regulators and payers ask whether a blood marker truly comes from the tumor — matched-tissue, spatially resolved data answers that.

industry.title: Specificity is the gap
industry.text: ProVue Lung shows high sensitivity but about **55% specificity**. Better tumor-specific markers, found in tissue, could lift specificity in a next version.

talking_points: After ProVue Lung, which cancers or diseases are next for biomarker discovery?
How do you confirm today that a plasma protein in your panel is really produced by the tumor and not by normal tissue or inflammation?
Your patent applies deep learning to raw MS data — would spatially labeled tissue samples (tumor vs stroma vs normal) be useful training data?
Your 682-feature model was narrowed to 11 proteins — would tissue-level, spatial data help choose markers for the next version, or improve specificity?
Do you have access to matched tissue (FFPE) from MOSAIC or the FDA-facing trial sites?
Who else should see Meteor's data — Manway Liu (data science), Yi Zeng (mass spec), the CTO or clinical?
What would a small first project look like when budget opens — a service pilot on a few tissue samples?
